title: Literature review of published ride acceleration measurements
context: RideBelt is an open, safety-critical Hee-Lee Oss project: an optional rider-worn backup restraint (low hip belt + short tethers; optional clip-on Shoulder Module or one-piece Integrated Harness) that latches into an open seat anchor standard (RAS). ALL safety content is DRAFT and not for use until a credentialed engineer signs off at the MVP gate (GOVERNANCE.md). Never remove a DRAFT banner, never give instructions for wearing or attaching anything to a ride, never copy text from paid standards (cite by number and title only), never name private individuals or incident victims, and respect the patent design-arounds in docs/research/patentability-fto.md. Peak values in ride-acceleration-data.md come from a handful of sources. Physics-education papers, injury-biomechanics studies and manufacturer statements contain many more.
objective: Build an annotated bibliography of published ride acceleration measurements, extracting peak +Gz, -Gz, Gx, Gy and durations per ride class into a table.
acceptanceCriteria: At least 15 sources, each with a link
Ride classes match the load-case classes in ride-acceleration-data.md
Flags where values exceed the current -2.0 g rating
Every factual claim has a cited, working source link; estimates are labelled as estimates
